title: .NET MAUI 11 Makes CoreCLR the Default Runtime and Adds Incremental XAML Hot Reload
gist: With .NET 11 (released 10 November, a two-year STS release), .NET MAUI switches its default runtime from Mono to CoreCLR on all platforms and adds incremental XAML hot reload, implicit XAML namespaces, lazy ResourceDictionary loading and more handler-based controls. The release consolidates rather than expands, raising Android's minimum API to 24, dropping x86, requiring iOS 18.2/Xcode 26.4, and introducing several breaking changes.

insights.claim: .NET MAUI in .NET 11 changes the default runtime from Mono to CoreCLR on all supported platforms, putting mobile and desktop apps on the same runtime as other .NET workloads.
insights.speaker: Edin Kapić
insights.so_what: Microsoft is unifying .NET on CoreCLR, de-emphasizing Mono — reduces fragmentation for cross-platform .NET developers.
insights.locator: The runtime switch is the most significant change.

insights.claim: In .NET MAUI 11, Release builds use composite partial ReadyToRun by default; on Apple platforms, which disallow JIT, non-precompiled code runs in the CoreCLR interpreter, while Native AOT is opt-in and still experimental on Android.
insights.speaker: Edin Kapić
insights.so_what: Developers must validate library compatibility per deployment model; Android Native AOT is not production-ready yet.
insights.locator: Release builds use composite partial ReadyToRun by default.

insights.claim: .NET 11 is a Standard Term Support release with two years of support, but .NET MAUI follows its own support policy separate from the runtime's STS/LTS lifecycle.
insights.speaker: Edin Kapić
insights.so_what: Enterprises planning MAUI upgrades should track MAUI's own support window, not the .NET runtime's.
insights.locator: .NET 11 is a Standard Term Support release

insights.claim: The .NET MAUI 11 release, built over seven previews and a release candidate with a stated focus on product quality, consolidates more than it expands, according to InfoQ's Edin Kapić.
insights.speaker: Edin Kapić
insights.so_what: MAUI is in a stabilization phase rather than a feature push — signals maturing, not expansion, of Microsoft's cross-platform UI bet.
insights.quote: Overall, this release consolidates more than it expands.

insights.claim: .NET MAUI 11 adds incremental XAML hot reload (in preview, on by default in Debug, works with dotnet watch) that patches live pages and controls without recreating them, and makes the root xmlns and xmlns:x declarations optional via implicit namespaces.
insights.speaker: Edin Kapić
insights.so_what: Faster inner-loop iteration narrows MAUI's developer-experience gap with competing cross-platform frameworks.

insights.claim: Lazy ResourceDictionary loading in .NET MAUI 11 makes large dictionaries initialize up to roughly eight times faster when XAML source generation is used, and RelativeSource bindings with a resolvable AncestorType now compile to trim-safe code.
insights.speaker: Edin Kapić
insights.so_what: Startup and trimming gains matter for mobile app size and performance.

insights.claim: For Android, .NET MAUI 11 release notes report an incremental build after a managed source change dropping from 68.3 to 52.3 seconds, and startup gains of 2.4% to 4.5% from partial ReadyToRun at the cost of a slightly larger package.
insights.speaker: Edin Kapić
insights.so_what: Modest but concrete build and startup improvements; size trade-off relevant to app-store-constrained apps.
insights.locator: The release notes report shorter builds

insights.claim: .NET MAUI 11 continues replacing legacy renderers with handlers — CollectionView2 by default on Windows, handler-based Android Shell, and handlers for NavigationPage, TabbedPage and FlyoutPage on iOS and Mac Catalyst — with old renderers kept as a manual fallback.
insights.speaker: Edin Kapić
insights.so_what: Migration away from Xamarin-era renderers is nearly complete, raising the cost of staying on legacy patterns.
insights.locator: Handlers keep replacing the legacy renderers

insights.claim: On iOS in .NET MAUI 11 the Appearing event now fires before a page is pushed rather than after it becomes visible, so developers depending on the old timing should switch to NavigatedTo.
insights.speaker: Edin Kapić
insights.so_what: A subtle behavioral change that can break navigation logic in existing apps during upgrade.
insights.locator: On iOS, Appearing now fires before a page is pushed

insights.claim: .NET MAUI 11 adds a Passkeys class in Microsoft.Maui.Authentication wrapping WebAuthn creation and assertion (servers must still validate challenges and attestation), plus map clustering, custom pin icons, an Azure Maps-backed Windows map, TabbedPage badges and Shell route templates.
insights.speaker: Edin Kapić
insights.so_what: Built-in passkey support lowers the barrier to passwordless auth in .NET mobile apps; Azure Maps integration pulls MAUI users toward Azure services.
insights.locator: Animation methods now accept a CancellationToken

insights.claim: .NET MAUI 11 raises the Android minimum API level from 21 to 24, drops x86 architecture support, and requires iOS, tvOS and Mac Catalyst 18.2, macOS 15.2 and Xcode 26.4 for Apple targets.
insights.speaker: Edin Kapić
insights.so_what: Apps serving older Android devices or x86 emulators/devices must stay on older MAUI or drop those users.
insights.locator: For Android, the minimum API level rises from 21 to 24

insights.claim: .NET MAUI 11 breaks existing code: the Microsoft.Maui.Controls.Compatibility package no longer ships, the Color record is sealed, Java.Lang.Object.JavaFinalize() is obsolete, non-font SwipeItem icons are no longer auto-tinted, and non-Async animation methods are obsolete; Microsoft advises thoroughly testing navigation, custom handlers and trimmed publishing.
insights.speaker: Edin Kapić
insights.so_what: Upgrade effort is non-trivial for apps relying on Xamarin compatibility shims — budget migration time.
